root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Finnish Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 dxe4 4. Nxe4 h6

overview: After 4.Nxe4 h6 Black prepares ...Bf5 without allowing Ng5, and keeps the usual Caro-Kann structure. White usually plays 5.Nf3 Bf5 6.Ng3 Bg6 and Black gets a solid, slightly passive position. White has more space, Black the sound structure.

white_ideas.idea: Trade the knight for the bishop to gain the pair

black_ideas.idea: Develop the bishop to f5 or g6 safely

typical_structures.structure: Caro-Kann structure with the c6 pawn and the bishop outside the chain

character.notes: Solid, steady play typical of the Caro-Kann.

structure.notes: Half-open d-file after the d-pawns come off.

level.notes: Plans are clear but need understanding.

character.reason: Typical Caro-Kann structure, hard to break.

structure.reason: The d-pawn exchange leaves a half-open file.

level.reason: Plans are clear, with subtlety in the move order.
